overview: Black answers 1.Nf3 d6 2.e4 with an early ...Bg4 pin, usually followed by ...Nf6, ...e6 and ...Nbd7, a modest Philidor-like set-up. White takes space with d4 and often meets ...Bxf3 with the bishop pair. Rare in serious play; the same structure arises from 1.e4 d6 2.Nf3 Bg4.

white_ideas.idea: Play d4 and Be2 or h3, building a broad centre.
Keep the bishop pair if Black takes on f3.

black_ideas.idea: Develop the c8 bishop outside the pawn chain with ...Bg4.
Hold d6 and e6, then break with ...e5 or ...c5.

typical_structures.structure: White e4/d4 centre against Black d6/e6 or d6/e5.

character.notes: Quiet development for both; no forcing theory, Black is slightly passive but not in danger.

soundness.notes: A playable, if slightly cramped, Philidor-type set-up; not refuted.

structure.notes: Centre not fixed: White e4 against d6 with ...e5 or ...c5 breaks still to come.

approach.notes: Seldom chosen by strong players; the Chigorin plan with ...Rb8 is eccentric.

level.notes: Little theory, but Black needs to judge when to take on f3 and how to free the position.

sublines_that_differ.name: Chigorin plan
sublines_that_differ.moves: 1. d4 d6 2. Nf3 Bg4 3. c4 Nd7 4. Qb3 Rb8
sublines_that_differ.how: A d4 move-order oddity with Black parking a rook on b8 against Qb3.

character.reason: Modest development on both sides, no forcing lines and no fortress.

soundness.reason: A passive but healthy Philidor-like set-up.

structure.reason: The centre stays undecided until Black chooses ...e5 or ...c5.

level.reason: Few lines to memorise but the set-up needs judgement.

plans.reason: White gets the bishop pair after ...Bxf3 and a bigger centre.
